name: MathlibAnnex.Satellite.absoluteMaximizer_satellite_norms_preimage
title: Each satellite norms its coefficient preimage in absolute value

content.display_title: Each satellite norms its coefficient preimage in absolute value
content.one_sentence_role: Varying one functional at an absolute maximizer forces endpoint attainment.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and use reference coordinates $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the sup norm. Let $p:V\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous seminorm with specified constants $a_p,b_p>0$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty\qquad(x\in V).$$
Thus $p$ is a norm. We use $p$ for the model distance and $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ for reference-coordinate estimates; the two norms are allowed to coincide. A $p$-dual contraction is a continuous real linear functional $r$ satisfying $|r(x)|\le p(x)$ for every $x$. Let $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ be the standard coordinate vectors. For an ordered family $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ of continuous real linear functionals on $V$, put
$$M_F=(\ell_i(e_j))_{i,j},\quad T_Fx=(\ell_i(x))_i=M_Fx,\quad
\mathcal U_p=\{F:\forall i,x,\ |\ell_i(x)|\le p(x)\}.$$
For a real number $\eta$, define the attained maximum and near-maximal set by
$$D_p=\max_{F\in\mathcal U_p}|\det M_F|>0,\qquad
\mathcal N_{p,\eta}=\{F\in\mathcal U_p:D_p-\eta\le|\det M_F|\}.$$
Admissibility is measured with $p$; the matrices are written in the fixed reference coordinates.

Let $J$ be a finite index set, possibly empty; choose coefficients $c_a\in V$ for $a\in J$. A configuration is a pair $Q=(F,s)$, where $F$ is a frame and $s=(s_a)_{a\in J}$ is a family of additional continuous real linear functionals, called satellites. Write
$$\Omega_p^J=\{(F,s):F\in\mathcal U_p,\ \forall a,x,\ |s_a(x)|\le p(x)\}.$$
For any real weight $w$, let $M_F[i\leftarrow r]$ replace row $i$ by $(r(e_j))_j$ and set
$$\Phi_{w,c}(F,s)=w\det M_F+\sum_{a\in J}\sum_{i=1}^n(c_a)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_a].$$
An absolute maximizer means a single $Q\in\Omega_p^J$ with $|\Phi_{w,c}(Q')|\le|\Phi_{w,c}(Q)|$ for every $Q'\in\Omega_p^J$. It need not maximize the signed polynomial. Suppose $\eta<D_p$ and the admissible absolute maximizer $Q=(F,s)$ also has $F\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta}$. For every fixed $a\in J$, put $z_a=M_F^{-1}c_a$. Then
$$|s_a(z_a)|=p(z_a).$$
content.assumptions: Finiteness of $J$, the positive comparison constants for $p$, the positive determinant gap, admissibility, near-maximality of the base, and absolute maximality are required. The weight is any real number. No positive-weight or budget assumption is added.
content.conclusion: Every satellite attains the norm in absolute value at its own coefficient preimage. This gives neither $s_a(z_a)=p(z_a)$ nor a common positive sign for all satellites.
content.proof_summary: Separate one satellite contribution, use dominated Hahn–Banach endpoints, and apply rigidity of an affine absolute maximum.

proof_steps.text:
**Keep the coefficient preimage visible.** Fix $a\in J$ and keep $z_a=M_F^{-1}c_a$ as in the statement. The gap gives $\det M_F\ne0$. Collect the terms that do not involve the $a$th satellite in
   $$R_a=w\det M_F+\sum_{b\ne a}\sum_i(c_b)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_b].$$
   For every replacement functional $r$, row Cramer for this same matrix and coefficient column gives
   $$\sum_i(c_a)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow r]
     =(\det M_F)r(M_F^{-1}c_a)=(\det M_F)\,r(z_a).$$
   Substituting just this row contribution into the polynomial gives
   $$\begin{aligned}
   \Phi_{w,c}(F,s[a\leftarrow r])&=R_a+(\det M_F)\,r(z_a),\\
   \Phi_{w,c}(F,s)&=R_a+(\det M_F)\,s_a(z_a).
   \end{aligned}$$
   This is the [one-satellite update formula](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L877-L894), with the same $F,c_a$ and nonzero determinant. Only the functional in position $a$ changes; $R_a$ and $z_a$ stay fixed. Admissibility gives $|s_a(z_a)|\le p(z_a)$.

**Supply the two norming endpoints at that same point.** The required functionals satisfy
   $$|r_\pm(x)|\le p(x)\quad(x\in V),\qquad
   r_+(z_a)=p(z_a),\quad r_-(z_a)=-p(z_a).$$
   If $z_a=0$, take both functionals to be zero. Otherwise define $h$ on the line $\mathbb Rz_a$ by $h(\beta z_a)=\beta p(z_a)$. Its domination is
   $$h(\beta z_a)=\beta p(z_a)\le|\beta|p(z_a)=p(\beta z_a).$$
   Apply [continuous seminorm-dominated Hahn–Banach extension](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/360da6fa66c1273b76b6b2d8c5666fd5ac2e3b56/Mathlib/Analysis/LocallyConvex/HahnBanach.lean#L69-L79) with subspace $\mathbb Rz_a$, this $h$, and continuous seminorm $p$. It gives a continuous linear extension $r_+$ with $r_+(x)\le p(x)$ for all $x$. Applying this inequality to $-x$ also gives $|r_+(x)|\le p(x)$. Moreover $r_+(z_a)=h(z_a)=p(z_a)$. Set $r_-=-r_+$. These are the functionals in [the norming endpoint lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L213-L224). Replacing only $s_a$ with either of them preserves every contraction condition, so both new configurations belong to $\Omega_p^J$.

**Compare the actual value with both endpoints.** Absolute maximality, applied to the two configurations from Step 2 and then to the formula in Step 1, gives
   $$\begin{aligned}
   |R_a+(\det M_F)\,p(z_a)|&\le|R_a+(\det M_F)\,s_a(z_a)|,\\
   |R_a-(\det M_F)\,p(z_a)|&\le|R_a+(\det M_F)\,s_a(z_a)|.
   \end{aligned}$$
   Since $p(z_a)\ge0$, the endpoint identity is
   $$\max\{|R_a+(\det M_F)\,p(z_a)|,|R_a-(\det M_F)\,p(z_a)|\}
   =|R_a|+|\det M_F|p(z_a).$$
   Combining it with the two comparisons and the triangle inequality yields
   $$\begin{aligned}
   |R_a|+|\det M_F|p(z_a)
   &\le|R_a+(\det M_F)\,s_a(z_a)|\\
   &\le|R_a|+|\det M_F|\,|s_a(z_a)|\\
   &\le|R_a|+|\det M_F|p(z_a).
   \end{aligned}$$
   All inequalities are equalities. Cancel $|R_a|$ and divide by $|\det M_F|>0$ to obtain $|s_a(z_a)|=p(z_a)$. This is [absolute affine endpoint rigidity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L770-L795) applied directly to the nonnegative number $p(z_a)$, the value $s_a(z_a)$, and these two endpoint comparisons. The case $p(z_a)=0$ is included.

content.lean_realization_notes: The [configuration polynomial](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L592-L595) evaluates $\Phi$ on a pair. [the product configuration type](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L539-L540), [satellite families](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L536-L536), [their contraction subset](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L543-L545) and [the admissible product set](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L548-L550) retain both components of $Q$. The [selected absolute maximizer](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L644-L647) is a choice from the compact product, not a uniqueness assertion. The proof-local scalar called `p` in the source is the number $p(z_a)$ here; it is not a second norm.
